findings.claim: the bifrost.md rollback paragraph pointed at the pre-apply dump without naming it, and that object can be overwritten or expire

verdict.text: f1 is fixed.
The pre-apply dump now sits under its own name in GCS.
Its size, MD5 and CRC32C match the 10:24:51 UTC original.
The component page names the object, says it is a whole-cluster dump to restore only `bifrost` from, and gives the correct delete date.
The fix broke nothing, and the stamp is green on this tree.
Gates: `loopctl gate stamp` from the worktree passed pre_commit, cli_tests and eval-row r1, with "stamp green: 7866ba40...".
That matches the fingerprint bound to this round's placeholder.

The object, listed read-only with the backup service account key from Vault: gs://localstack-cluster-backups/postgres-pre-upgrade/bifrost-2.0.0-pgdumpall-2026-10-20.sql.gz has Content-Length 1399446141, MD5 uTfank6V9fcIQGtAWWsA6w== and CRC32C dHwmRg==, the same as postgres/pgdumpall-2026-10-20.sql.gz, which was created at 10:24:51 UTC.
The copy was created at 10:32:20 UTC.
Delete date: deployments/infrastructure/storage.tf has one bucket-wide lifecycle rule (age 180, Delete) with no prefix condition.
Age counts from the copy's own creation on 2026-10-20, and 2026-10-20 plus 180 days is 2027-04-18, so the page is right.
I could not read the live bucket's config, because the service account lacks storage.buckets.get.
The Terraform resource and docs/reference/gcs-backups.md agree on the rule.
"A name no job writes": backup-postgres runs `rclone copy` into `postgres/` only.
backup-s3 runs `rclone sync` into `minio/<bucket>/` prefixes only, so no sync can delete objects under `postgres-pre-upgrade/`.
Nothing else in deployments/ writes to the bucket.
The diff of .okf/components/bifrost.md against main: the new paragraph is correct, and the rest of the version-history paragraph matches round 1.
f1: resolved.
.okf/components/bifrost.md:149-158 names the copied object, says it is a whole-cluster dump to restore only `bifrost` from, and gives the 2027-04-18 delete date.
The object exists and matches the original.
The 180-day rule will delete the copy on 2027-04-18.
If 2.0.0 might still be needed after that date, someone has to move the copy somewhere else.
